message: an rgba() colour isn't supported in Outlook Windows (3 places)
hint: Those clients ignore it; drop the property or narrow --targets.

message: border-radius isn't supported in Outlook Windows; partly in Yahoo! Mail Desktop Webmail, Yahoo! Mail iOS, Yahoo! Mail Android (14 places)
hint: Round corners can be used in VML with the `RoundRect` element. See the [VML documentation](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/vml/msdn-online-vml-roundrect-element).

message: padding is only partly supported in Outlook Windows (2 places)
hint: Partial. Only supported on table cells.

message: linear-gradient() isn't supported in Outlook Windows, Outlook.com, Yahoo! Mail Desktop Webmail, Yahoo! Mail iOS, Yahoo! Mail Android; partly in Gmail Android
hint: Gradients can be created in VML using `type="gradient"` on a `<v:fill>`. See [VML documentation](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/vml/web-workshop---how-to-use-vml-on-web-pages-----fill--element#gradient-fill).

message: Text at 11px is very small (4 places)
hint: Under 12px is hard to read on phones; 14px or more is the usual floor for body text.

message: Text at 10px is very small (2 places)
hint: Under 12px is hard to read on phones; 14px or more is the usual floor for body text.

message: align-items: center can't center text by its content size; use text-align
hint: Tables can't express this exactly, so the email will differ slightly from the browser here.

message: align-items: baseline is approximated as top (4 places)
hint: Tables can't express this exactly, so the email will differ slightly from the browser here.

message: flex-grow on a calc() flex-basis is ignored; the item keeps its calc() width (4 places)
hint: This only matters when its line has room left over; if the line is already full, flex: 0 0 calc(...) says the same thing. A px flex-basis lets an item grow.

message: shorter items' backgrounds won't stretch (2 places)
hint: Only full-width boxes can stretch to the row's height in email; drop the item's width or align it to the top.

message: Outlook shows the gradient's first colour, #6b5e4c
hint: There's no email-safe way to keep this exactly, so td;dr left it out or used the closest safe form.

message: overflow: hidden cuts the line off in most clients; Outlook ignores it, so the line may wrap or stretch the table there
hint: Outlook Windows has no overflow clipping. Keep the content within the width, or accept that Outlook shows all of it.

message: Outlook shows the background colour; set a px min-height to get the photo in Outlook
hint: Outlook draws a background photo through VML, which needs a px width and height.
